As a former small biz owner in a past lifetime…(auto diagnostics for 25 years. Honest) It was getting so hard to make a decent profit even back then. Had 4 high tech employees, plus myself, (for total of 5) workers comp insurance, shop insurance, rent, utilities, benefits for employees, taxes…etc. Bad weather killed us ..snowstorms, flooding. Back then credit cards were charging me 1.6% and AMEX was 2.7%..I feel for the small biz man today. Almost impossible to make a decent profit. Then you had state auditors checking receipts for sales taxes, Insurance checking salaries and job descriptions for workers comp insurance. Every so often I would get a letter from the IRS..”you owe 675.00 plus interest from 3 years ago!”. BS but had to pay. Just look at all the businesses today. Mostly huge chains all over.

In my area, Acme grocery is owned by Safeway, Stop and Shop is owned by a European company, same with Lidl etc.. After selling a decent profit, I joined the NYPD with free benefits!! Retired now. But still with all those great benefits.

Most folks don’t even know the cost of doing business. Sorry for being wordy but those are the facts.

Plus a friend in the gasoline biz had a pump out of order. 1800 to repair it, not even mentioning the drivers who drive off with the nozzle still in the gas filler!! 300 to replace!!

I know the cost of doing business. Not my problem. I’m on this site to make money for churning credit cards with rewards and bank bonuses. Not interested in excuses that will eventually sunset this activity. Not sure why you people are here. Go after big brother red tape instead on backdooring to eliminate these rewards for the average person.

To be fair, the first reason might be legitimate. The other 3 are BS.

Lack of an open installment dings your FICO 25-35 points. That would be the main reason your score was low.

Another cause of an unexpectedly low score is zero CCs reporting a balance on the day they happen to pull your report. A $1+ balance reporting on 1 card solves that. $3 to be safe, in case of small balance waivers.

Partially because of the Paze promo, I have about 10 cards reporting a balance. In fact, I am thinking the opposite… It looks bad to have that many active.

Total available revolving credit is almost $300K. I have 30 open CC’s, with a total “debt” balance of about $500-$1000, depending on the snapshot they took. I really think I need to start closing out some “duplicate” cards I have…

PNC recently closed my $1K LOC that I had open for over 20 years, closed due to inactivity (never used it – it was opened as overdraft protection). That was my only open non-revolving account.

That score doesn’t feel right to me, regardless. I pulled my FICO via Bank of America just now. 788/850. Uses Experian. Discover uses Transunion, and showing an 800 FICO for 8/27/26. Barclays, the same score, for 08/16/2026.

Free FICO’s: https://www.doctorofcredit.com/comparison-free-fico-scores-banks-cus/

10/30 is too many accounts with balances, but no way could that account for a 60+ point change. Not even close.

You can have up to 21% of cards showing small balances with no effect on FICO 8. So with 30 open cards, anywhere from 1-6 balances would be optimal. But again, a 60 point drop for 10/30 would be ridiculous.

I wonder if BMO is using a different scoring model. Did they mention which version? BoA, Barclays and Discover are all FICO 8 (the most common).

Wells Fargo gives a FICO 9 score (albeit EX) and US Bank uses FICO 10 so maybe you could compare those.

Or possibly BMO was using an internal score, like Chase? I’d love to know where they got that score, it just seems ludicrous.

This has been a pain point for me and I have spent a lot of time coming up with solutions — a couple of options: 1) check if your utilities allow you to pay with a debit card without a fee; often can do very small amounts for electricity, phone bill, etc. 2) if you use E-ZPass (or your local equivalent) for tolls, I have loaded as little as $2.12 before. 3) if you have a Target gift card balance, you can adjust the amount used from the balance and then split payment with another card; so if your total is $9.99, use $5.53 of your available Target GC balance, leaving exactly $4.46 left to pay, then use the MC GC for that — it will drain it to $0.00… have successfully done it for $0.10! (just be careful if your area charges for plastic bags at pick up, my Targets automatically charge $0.50 for 10 bags and then refund you based on the number actually used; not an issue for orders that are shipped). Good luck!

RockAuto info:
Can I use multiple payment methods on one order?
Yes (up to four, not counting Gift Certificates/Store Credits). Check the “Split Payment” box, select your first payment method, enter its information and the amount you wish to be applied to it, and click “Add Payment”. Then repeat to specify other payment method(s) for the remaining balance.

Your payments will be shown in the “Payments” section. Click remove next to a method if you decide not to use it.

To specify a payment method for the remaining balance (shown in the “Amount” box), choose the method, enter in any necessary information, and click “Place Order”.
